newsitem.title: USA: Galileo sees offer proceeds of $275.6 mln.
newsitem.headline: Galileo sees offer proceeds of $275.6 mln.

text.p: Galileo International Inc said Thursday it expects to receive about $275.6 million in net proceeds from its initial public offering.
The funds will be used to acquire computerized reservation systems.
Proceeds will increase to $387 million if the underwriters' over-allotment option is exercised in full.

The financing will be used for the acquisitions of Apollo Travel Services Partnership (ATS) from United Airlines, US Airways Group Inc and Air Canada ; Galileo Nederland B.V. from KLM Royal Dutch Airlines ; and Traviswiss A.G. from SAirGroup.

ATS, Galileo Nederland and Traviswiss are each national distribution companies for Galileo International's global distribution system products. The remaining net proceeds will go to the selling shareholders.
Galileo allows travel agencies at about 36,000 locations to access schedule and fare information, book reservations and issue tickets for 525 airlines.

The initial public offering of 31,998,000 shares of common stock was priced at $24.50 a share. The offering amounts to $784 million. At the offering price, Galileo will have a market value of $2.45 billion.

Underwriters are led by Morgan Stanley Dean Witter. Lehman Brothers, Merrill Lynch & Co, J.P. Morgan, and SBC Warburg Inc are co- managers in the U.S. offering. International underwriters for the offering will be led by Morgan Stanley Dean Witter., SBC Warburg, a division of Swiss Bank Corporation, ABN AMRO Rothschild, HSBC Investment Banking, Lehman Brothers, Merrill Lynch International, and J.P. Morgan Securities Ltd.
